## Introduction{.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
### The Context
As Artificial Intelligence transitions from experimental phases to core enterprise integration in 2025, the career trajectories and compensation structures have evolved dramatically.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
### Core Questions
This project maps out a global roadmap to answer three pivotal questions:

- **The Experience Premium**: How much financial growth does career progression yield?
- **Golden Skills**: Which specific technical skills serve as the highest-valued currency?
- **Geographical Arbitrage**: Which locations offer the maximum return?
:::

:::

## Salary Trajectories by Experiences{.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%" .smaller}

- **The Premium: ** Median salaries more than *double* from Entry to Executive.
- **High Ceiling: **  Executive compensation shows massive variance—the sky is the limit.
:::

::: {.column width="70%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-experience
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# Load Data
ai_data <- read_csv("data/ai_job_dataset.csv") 

# Data Cleaning
ai_data_clean <- ai_data %>%
  mutate(experience_level = factor(experience_level, 
                                   levels = c("EN", "MI", "SE", "EX"),
                                   labels = c("Entry", "Mid-level", "Senior", "Executive")))

# Plot
ggplot(ai_data_clean, aes(x = experience_level, y = salary_usd, fill = experience_level)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, color = "#444444", outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", color = "darkred", size = 2) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1/1000, suffix = "K")) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Salary Distribution by Experience",
    subtitle = "AI compensation ceilings rise sharply at Executive level",
    x = "Career Stage",
    y = "Annual Salary (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Global AI Job Market Dataset 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray30"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.8, y = 420000, label = "High variance at\nExecutive level", 
           color = "darkred", size = 2.5, fontface = "italic")
```
:::
:::

## High-Value Roles: Job Category Compensation {.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}

- **Top Earners: **
  Research and Engineering roles command the highest median salaries

- **Market Standard: **
  Most mainstream AI categories cluster around a healthy competitive range, showing robust baseline compensation across the industry.

:::

::: {.column width="70%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-job-category
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "right"

ai_data_jobs <- ai_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(job_title)) %>%
  mutate(job_category = fct_reorder(job_title, salary_usd, .fun = median))

ggplot(ai_data_jobs, aes(x = job_category, y = salary_usd, fill = job_category)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "bar", alpha = 0.8, width = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = median, 
    geom = "text", 
    aes(label = sprintf("$%.0fK", ..y../1000)), 
    hjust = -0.1, 
    size = 2.5, 
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray15"
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_dollar(scale = 1/1000, suffix = "K"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)) 
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Annual Salary by Job Category",
    subtitle = "Technical research and infrastructure roles lead the market",
    x = "Job Category",
    y = "Median Annual Salary (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Global AI Job Market Dataset 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```
:::
:::

## High-Valued Technical Skills {.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}

- **Premium Capabilities: **
  Advanced engineering skills like MLOps, Distributed Systems, and Large Language Models command higher average compensation.

- **Market Baseline: **
  Foundational skills (e.g., Python, SQL) have narrower intervals due to higher sample sizes
:::

::: {.column width="70%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-skills
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"


ai_skills_summary <- ai_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(required_skills)) %>%
  separate_rows(required_skills, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(required_skills = str_trim(required_skills)) %>%
  filter(required_skills != "") %>%
  group_by(required_skills) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_salary = mean(salary_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_salary = sd(salary_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  slice_max(count, n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    se = sd_salary / sqrt(count),
    margin_error = 1.96 * se,
    ci_lower = mean_salary - margin_error,
    ci_upper = mean_salary + margin_error,
    required_skills = fct_reorder(required_skills, mean_salary)
  )


ggplot(ai_skills_summary, aes(x = required_skills, y = mean_salary, color = required_skills)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1/1000, suffix = "K")) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 AI Skills by Mean Annual Salary",
    subtitle = "Points show sample means; error bars represent 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Required Skill",
    y = "Average Annual Salary (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Global AI Job Market Dataset 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
:::
:::


## Geographical Arbitrage: Global Salary Disparities {.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%"}

- **Nordic Paradox: **
  Certain Nordic markets edge out the US in *overall median* salary. 
  
- **Specialized Sample: **
  This anomaly is driven by high welfare baselines and data limited to senior expert samples in those regions.
:::

::: {.column width="75%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-geography
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"


ai_geo_data <- ai_data %>%
  mutate(company_location = str_trim(company_location)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(company_location) & company_location != "") %>%
  mutate(
    company_location = case_when(
      company_location == "United State" ~ "United States",
      TRUE ~ company_location
    ),
    experience_level = factor(experience_level, 
                             levels = c("EN", "MI", "SE", "EX"),
                             labels = c("Entry", "Mid-level", "Senior", "Executive"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(experience_level))

top_3_countries <- ai_geo_data %>%
  group_by(company_location) %>%
  summarise(med_salary = median(salary_usd, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice_max(med_salary, n = 3) %>%
  pull(company_location)

ai_geo_data <- ai_geo_data %>%
  mutate(
    highlight_color = case_when(
      company_location == top_3_countries[1] ~ "Rank 1",
      company_location == top_3_countries[2] ~ "Rank 2",
      company_location == top_3_countries[3] ~ "Rank 3",
      TRUE ~ "Other Countries"
    ),
    highlight_color = factor(highlight_color, levels = c("Rank 1", "Rank 2", "Rank 3", "Other Countries"))
  )


unique_countries <- sort(unique(ai_geo_data$company_location))
axis_font_faces <- ifelse(unique_countries %in% top_3_countries, "bold", "plain")


ggplot(ai_geo_data, aes(x = company_location, y = salary_usd, fill = highlight_color)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.alpha = 0.2, width = 0.6, color = "#444444") +
  facet_wrap(~ experience_level, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1/1000, suffix = "K")) +
  
 
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Rank 1" = "#E05650",       
      "Rank 2" = "#2D8B93",       
      "Rank 3" = "#E6A15C",       
      "Other Countries" = "#EAEAEA" 
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Global AI Salary Disparities: Top 3 Markets Highlighted",
    subtitle = "Identify the top 3 highest-paying countries",
    x = "Company Location",
    y = "Annual Salary (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Global AI Job Market Dataset 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7, angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = axis_font_faces), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, color = "gray10"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
:::
:::


## Conclusion: Core Insights {.smaller}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 1. Structured Advancement

- **Predictable Paths: **
  AI compensation is highly structured. Median salaries more than *double* from Entry to Executive tiers.

- **Market Density: **
  Senior (SE) roles represent the stablest and most densely populated high-income talent pool.

- **Role Premium: **
  Research and Infrastructure Engineering command the highest median baselines over generalist roles.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 2. Multipliers & Anomalies

- **Skills Currency: **
  Specialization acts as a multiplier. MLOps, Distributed Systems, and LLMs yield the highest financial returns.

- **Geographic Power: **
  Company location heavily dictates pay. 

- **Nordic Paradox: **
  Certain Nordic markets present a counter-intuitive median premium, driven by senior-heavy expert samples.
:::

:::
